knowledge:
- key_parameters: mir_predicted_targets=A matrix of prior target predictions (e.g., TargetScan) with genes in rows and miRNAs in columns, or NULL to use all miRNA-gene interactions ;; mscor.threshold=The minimum sensitivity correlation threshold used to filter the ceRNA network ;; padj.threshold=The adjusted p-value threshold used to filter the ceRNA network for statistical significance ;; method=The single-sample gene set enrichment approach used in enrichment_modules, with options "OE" (Overall Enrichment), "ssGSEA", or "GSVA" ;; threshold=The coefficient threshold (default -0.05) in sponge_gene_miRNA_interaction_filter to retain only miRNAs that repress gene expression
- alternatives: Conditional mutual information or partial correlation methods (e.g., using ppcor directly without SPONGE's filtering and null model) ;; F-test instead of elastic net regression in sponge_gene_miRNA_interaction_filter to identify important miRNAs
- when_to_use: Paired gene and miRNA expression data are available for the same samples and you want to identify significant ceRNA interactions or construct a ceRNA network ;; You want to calculate sample-specific ceRNA module scores (spongEffects) for downstream classification, even on cohorts lacking miRNA data
- pitfalls: Gene and miRNA identifiers in the interaction matrices must match the format of those in the expression matrices ;; Samples must be ordered identically in both expression matrices and each sample must have an entry in both ;; Precision of empirical p-values is limited by the number of datasets sampled in the null model (e.g., 100 datasets limits the best p-value to 0.01; 1e6 is recommended) ;; Each parallel worker in foreach requires a copy of the data, which can cause memory issues unless bigmemory description objects are used

workflows.name: cerna_network_inference
workflows.intent: Identify significant ceRNA interactions and construct a ceRNA network from paired gene and miRNA expression data.
input: gene_expr (matrix of gene expression with samples in rows and genes in columns)
mir_expr (matrix of miRNA expression with samples in rows and miRNAs in columns)
targetscan_symbol (matrix of predicted miRNA-gene interactions with genes in rows and miRNAs in columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter gene-miRNA interactions using regularized regression ;; 2. Compute sensitivity correlation (mscor) for gene pairs ;; 3. Build null model for p-value computation ;; 4. Compute empirical p-values and adjust for multiple testing ;; 5. Filter for significant interactions and plot network/centralities
workflows.code:
genes_miRNA_candidates <- sponge_gene_miRNA_interaction_filter(
gene_expr = gene_expr,
mir_expr = mir_expr,
mir_predicted_targets = targetscan_symbol)

ceRNA_interactions <- sponge(gene_expr = gene_expr,
                        mir_expr = mir_expr,
                        mir_interactions = genes_miRNA_candidates)

mscor_null_model <- sponge_build_null_model(number_of_datasets = 100, number_of_samples = nrow(gene_expr))

sponge_plot_simulation_results(mscor_null_model)

ceRNA_interactions_sign <- sponge_compute_p_values(sponge_result = ceRNA_interactions, 
                                                   null_model = mscor_null_model)

ceRNA_interactions_fdr <- ceRNA_interactions_sign[which(ceRNA_interactions_sign$p.adj < 0.2),]

sponge_plot_network(ceRNA_interactions_fdr, genes_miRNA_candidates)

network_centralities <- sponge_node_centralities(ceRNA_interactions_fdr)

ceRNA_interactions_fdr_weight <- ceRNA_interactions_fdr
ceRNA_interactions_fdr_weight$weight <- -log10(ceRNA_interactions_fdr$p.adj)
weighted_network_centralities <- sponge_node_centralities(ceRNA_interactions_fdr)

sponge_plot_network_centralities(weighted_network_centralities, top = 1)

sponge_plot_network_centralities(weighted_network_centralities, measure = "btw", top = 1)

workflows.name: sponge_effects_classification
workflows.intent: Define ceRNA modules, calculate enrichment scores per sample, and train/validate a subtype classification model.
input: train_cancer_gene_expr (matrix of gene expression for training)
test_cancer_gene_expr (matrix of gene expression for testing)
train_ceRNA_interactions (data frame of pre-computed ceRNA interactions)
train_cancer_metadata (data frame of sample metadata for training)
test_cancer_metadata (data frame of sample metadata for testing)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter ceRNA network and compute weighted centralities ;; 2. Identify central nodes/modules ;; 3. Define SPONGE modules ;; 4. Calculate enrichment scores per sample ;; 5. Calibrate classification model ;; 6. Predict on test set and evaluate
workflows.code:
filtered_network_centralities=filter_ceRNA_network(sponge_effects = train_ceRNA_interactions, Node_Centrality = train_network_centralities,add_weighted_centrality=T, mscor.threshold = 0.01, padj.threshold = 0.1)

RNAs <- c("lncRNA","protein_coding")
RNAs.ofInterest <- ensembl.df %>% dplyr::filter(gene_biotype %in% RNAs) %>%
  dplyr::select(ensembl_gene_id)

central_gene_modules<-get_central_modules(central_nodes = RNAs.ofInterest$ensembl_gene_id,node_centrality = filtered_network_centralities$Node_Centrality,ceRNA_class = RNAs, centrality_measure = "Weighted_Degree", cutoff = 10)

Sponge.modules <- define_modules(network = filtered_network_centralities$Sponge.filtered, central.modules = central_gene_modules, remove.central = F, set.parallel = F)
# Module size distribution
Size.modules <- sapply(Sponge.modules, length)

train.modules <- enrichment_modules(Expr.matrix = train_cancer_gene_expr, modules = Sponge.modules, bin.size = 10, min.size = 1, max.size = 2000, min.expr = 1, method = "OE", cores=1)
test.modules <-  enrichment_modules(Expr.matrix = test_cancer_gene_expr, modules = Sponge.modules, bin.size = 10, min.size = 1, max.size = 2000, min.expr = 1, method = "OE", cores=1)

# We find modules that were identified both in the train and test and use those as input features for the model
common_modules = intersect(rownames(train.modules), rownames(test.modules))
train.modules = train.modules[common_modules, ]
test.modules = test.modules[common_modules, ]

trained.model = calibrate_model(Input = train.modules, modules_metadata = train_cancer_metadata, label = "SUBTYPE", sampleIDs = "sampleID",Metric = "Exact_match", n_folds = 2, repetitions = 1)

Input.test <- t(test.modules) %>% scale(center = T, scale = T)
Prediction.model <- predict(trained.model$Model, Input.test)

# We compute the confusion metrix on the test set
ConfusionMatrix_testing <- caret::confusionMatrix(as.factor(Prediction.model), as.factor(test_cancer_metadata$SUBTYPE))
trained.model$ConfusionMatrix_testing<-ConfusionMatrix_testing
